conclusion: The measured transient comparison ran successfully, but plant validation is not established. Geometry, thermal storage and instrument uncertainties remain incompletely specified; all measured-response discrepancies are retained.

experiment.plant: Krško, Westinghouse two-loop PWR, post-2000 uprate, core cycle 21
experiment.eventTimeConvention: Report section 4: t=0 is the inferred start of governor-valve closure, 53 seconds after the source acquisition began.
experiment.windowRationale: End before operator reopening at approximately 16 s and inferred SI/reactor trip at approximately 17 s. The report warns that post-trip neutron-power and flow indications do not directly represent total decay heat and actual flows; those intervals are excluded.
experiment.measurementTimingAllowanceBasis: Half of the reported 2 s acquisition interval; a comparison allowance, not a quantified instrument-delay distribution.

extraction.method: Read PDF vector vertices of the magenta measured instrument curve in panel (a); exclude blue curves labeled cal and all legend symbols.
extraction.timeRounding: Vector x-coordinates match -49,-47,...,49 s within 0.06 s. They are snapped to that stated acquisition grid; values are rounded to six decimals for reproducibility, not six-digit measurement accuracy.
extraction.readingAllowance: A conservative half-PDF-point vertical reading allowance is recorded per channel by the extractor. It is roughly 0.006 MPa for primary pressure, 0.005 MPa for SG pressure, 0.04 K for cold legs and 0.13 K for hot legs. It covers figure extraction only, not instrument uncertainty.
extraction.pressureAxisCorrection: Figures 29,33,34 label pressure in MPa but print bar-valued ticks (primary 144–162; SG 64–80). Multiply these tick values by 0.1 to recover MPa. This is corroborated independently by measured Table 2 initial pressure 15.48 MPa and SG pressures 6.42/6.40 MPa; raw printed values must not be treated as 154.8 MPa or 64.2 MPa.
extraction.aggregation: Hot/cold temperatures and SG pressures are unweighted means of the two reported loop instruments. Steam and feedwater flows are sums. These means do not resolve loop asymmetry.
extraction.powerConversion: Before trip, reported neutron power percent multiplied by 1994 MW / 100. It is a thermal-input proxy, not direct calorimetry and not a valid post-trip decay-heat measurement.

initialConditions.basis: Measured t=0 column of Table 2 (printed page 13, PDF page 25), with arithmetic means for two-loop temperatures and pressure.

calibrationAndHoldout.initializationData: Only Table 2 initial values calibrate the nominal heat-transfer conductances and feedwater enthalpy needed for constructed equilibrium.
calibrationAndHoldout.parameterFitting: No transient response channel is used to fit volumes, heat capacities, conductances, control gains or time constants. No optimization is performed.
calibrationAndHoldout.acceptance: No plant-validation acceptance band is asserted: the source does not supply instrument uncertainties or the complete plant geometry/input deck needed for this reduced model. Errors are reported even when large. Numerical success does not turn the applicability assessment into a validation pass.

limitations: This is a short, boundary-driven thermal/inventory comparison. Measured core power and secondary flows are inputs, so the test does not validate neutron kinetics, turbine controls, generator, feedwater controls or trip logic.

The primary hot/cold volumes, fuel heat capacity, pressurizer volume, and secondary volume remain generic assumptions scaled from OpenPWR by initial core thermal power/3000 MW. They are not identified Krško geometry.
A homogeneous equilibrium secondary model omits distributed boiling, subcooled feedwater mixing, SG walls and instrument shrink/swell. The primary model omits wall heat storage and transport delays.

Initial feedwater enthalpy is inferred from a zero initial secondary energy-rate balance because inlet enthalpy is not given in the selected report. The measured feedwater/steam mismatch is retained, so initial secondary mass inventory need not be exactly stationary.
The reported 6 MW pump heat is omitted by the reused primary model. This is a known discrepancy, not an adjusted fit parameter.

Pressurizer heater, spray, charging and letdown are fixed to zero in this scoped replay. Figures 31–32 contain charging/letdown volumetric-flow curves, but their reference conditions and incoming-water enthalpy have not been established here. Their omission limits interpretation of the primary-pressure discrepancy.

The pre-event figure curves indicate aggregate steam flow around 1003 kg/s and feedwater around 996 kg/s, while Table 2 lists roughly the reverse. Instrument identifiers in Table 3 and captions are followed without swapping, offsetting or fitting the curves. The inconsistency remains a source-input limitation.
Instrument calibration accuracy and delay distributions are unavailable; graphical reading allowances cannot replace them.
The published curves are a rendered representation of measurements, not the original raw acquisition dataset.

numericalEvidence.initialPoint: t=0 is linearly interpolated from the figure; excluded from error statistics and retained to show initialization bias.
numericalEvidence.scope: Independent boundary integrals, communication-step refinement and explicitly uncalibrated volume/capacity sensitivity. These are numerical diagnostics, not uncertainty propagation or physical acceptance tests.
